items.headline: Hidden Microsoft Copilot Features You Should Be Using
items.summary: Scheduled prompts are among the most underused Microsoft Copilot features, running questions automatically on daily, weekly, or monthly cadences and surfacing results when needed. Custom Instructions shape how Copilot responds while memory retains commonly referenced details across interactions, making prompts shorter, responses clearer, and drafts requiring less editing. The Researcher Agent automates research heavy lifting through comparative analyses and comprehensive reports with infographics, citations and summaries.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's 150+ Microsoft certified experts and Power Platform practice can use scheduled prompts and Researcher Agent capabilities to accelerate client delivery across our Microsoft Fabric engagements. Share this with the Microsoft practice team and incorporate scheduled prompt workflows into our AI Discovery & Assessment Workshops, particularly for Manufacturing and Financial Services clients automating compliance reporting and operational intelligence.

items.headline: The Meta Instagram Breach: How AI Chatbots Became a Security Liability
items.summary: Meta confirmed over 20,000 Instagram accounts were compromised through a vulnerability in its AI-powered support chatbot between April 17 and early June 2026. The EY Canada hallucination incident produced a report with fabricated statistics, broken references, fake URLs, and a completely made-up McKinsey study. Q1 2026 saw U.S. courts issue $145,000 in sanctions against attorneys who filed AI-generated false citations, the highest quarterly total in legal history, with researcher Damien Charlotin cataloguing over 1,353 such cases globally.
items.levelshiftAngle: These failures validate LevelShift's Controlled Execution methodology (Phase 5 of our 5-Phase Framework) and our SOC 2 and CMMI certifications as trust signals. The EY hallucination incident proves why governance playbooks and human-in-the-loop services matter before AI goes to production. Use these as battle cards in pipeline conversations: Meta chatbot breach demonstrates the security risks of rushing AI deployment without proper testing, while EY and legal hallucinations show why our AI governance frameworks prevent exactly these failure modes. Reference our SOC 2 certification when Financial Services and Healthcare prospects raise security concerns.

items.headline: AI Act enforcement gets independent expert support
items.summary: The European Commission appointed a 60-member Scientific Panel and Advisory Forum on June 1, 2026, to support AI Act enforcement, advising the Commission's AI Office and national authorities on applying rules. Full Article 50 enforcement begins August 2, 2026, with transparency obligations for AI-generated content marking and labeling. Fines can reach EUR 35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for violations related to general-purpose AI models, with the final Code of Practice on synthetic content due in June 2026.
